question: Did northern Europeans and East African herders inherit their adult milk digestion from shared ancestors?
answer: No. Each population carries its own mutation, arisen separately within the last several thousand years, yet they sit in the same short stretch of DNA: a switch that normally turns the lactase gene off after weaning. Evolution flipped that one switch several separate times, wherever people kept animals for milk.
move: The same solution twice can mean the same problem twice, not shared descent.
ask: When two people or groups share a habit, do I assume they share a past or just a problem?
reference: Tishkoff, Reed, Ranciaro et al., Convergent adaptation of human lactase persistence in Africa and Europe, Nature Genetics, 2007
